title: Brookings Institution Report: Over 100,000 Family Separations in Trump Crackdown
partialText: The Brookings Institution suggests that federal statistics are an undercount because immigrant parents are not being asked about or not disclosing their American children.

title: How a Funding Pause Derailed an Artificial Heart for Babies
partialText: James Antaki’s efforts to develop a baby’s heart were close to success when his federal funding was cut off. The grants were eventually restored; rebuilding what was lost wasn’t so easy.

title: Trump’s Approval Sinks Amid Unpopular War, Darkening G.O.P. Prospects
partialText: With the midterms nearing, President Trump’s approval rating has hit a second-term low as voters question his handling of the economy, according to the latest New York Times/Siena poll.

title: A Crack in the Polling Floor Puts Trump in New Territory
partialText: A 37 percent approval rating in a new Times/Siena poll suggests the G.O.P. is facing a big midterm problem despite recent redistricting gains.

title: Why Did Some LIRR Unions Decide to Strike?
partialText: Members of the five unions that are on strike made more than $136,000 last year on average, according to M.T.A. figures. But they have not received a raise since 2022.

title: Tonys 2026 Predictions: Who Will Win? And Who Should?
partialText: Our chief theater critic looks at this year’s nominees and makes some predictions (and recommendations).

title: How the Music of ‘Schmigadoon!’ Echoes Broadway’s Past
partialText: The composer Cinco Paul discusses the clever references to classic musicals everywhere you look (and hear) in his new Broadway show.

title: Indictment and Impeachment Only Made Him Stronger. Remind You of Anyone?
partialText: The fate of Ken Paxton, the conservative Texas firebrand, could decide whether Republicans keep control of the Senate.

title: In Closed-Door Talks, U.S. Demands a Major Role in Greenland
partialText: Greenlandic officials worry about the direction of the negotiations aimed at defusing President Trump’s threats to seize their island. But they have little leverage.

title: Trump’s Taiwan Gambit is Already a Gift to China
partialText: President Trump’s open willingness to hold up a $14 billion Taiwan arms package is a win for Beijing. Now China could be weighing how to keep the weapons on ice for as long as it can.

title: Catastrophe Is Emerging in the World’s Most Vulnerable Places
partialText: The humanitarian relief system, decimated by cuts, faces a grave challenge as the Middle East war causes soaring costs for food, fuel and fertilizer.

title: Actually, Democracy Dies in H.R.
partialText: New research sheds light on how mediocre employees help would-be authoritarians maintain power.

title: Trump Warns Iran the ‘Clock Is Ticking’ as Tensions Surge Again in Middle East
partialText: The president has sought to force Iran to accept his terms on its nuclear program or else face renewed war. An emboldened Iran has rebuffed Trump’s demands.

title: Blocked Strait of Hormuz Leads to New Opportunities for Syria
partialText: The latest war in the Middle East has created new economic opportunities for Syria thanks to its geography.

title: Gun Found in Mangione’s Backpack Can be Used as Evidence, Judge Says
partialText: The ruling was a partial victory for prosecutors in the murder trial of Luigi Mangione. A state judge ruled that some other material and statements could not be used.

title: What to Know About the Latest Ebola Outbreak
partialText: The World Health Organization declared a global health emergency after about 80 people died from the virus in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

title: Americans Are Among Those Affected by Ebola Outbreak, C.D.C. Says
partialText: A small number of U.S. citizens have been directly affected by the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda, the C.D.C. said on Sunday.

title: He Shut Liquor Stores and Banned Abortion, All for the Glory of Russia
partialText: A firebrand governor aims to transform his region into a laboratory for the Kremlin’s reactionary ideals.

title: Russia’s New Human Rights Commissioner Accused of Helping Kidnap Ukrainian Children
partialText: Yana Lantratova was instrumental in helping the chairman of her party to illegally adopt an infant girl from Russian-occupied Ukraine, the Ukrainian authorities say.

title: Mamdani’s First City-Owned Grocery Store Is Planned for the South Bronx
partialText: Mayor Zohran Mamdani said that the store will open in the Hunts Point neighborhood next year. Some merchants are pushing back.

title: Trump Has Done More Than Misjudge Iran
partialText: The war has revealed the true puniness of Trump’s power

title: The Fighting Never Ends
partialText: We look at what happens when countries say they’re going to stop shooting at each other.

title: Federal Prosecutors Move to Drop Bribery Case Against Indian Magnate
partialText: Gautam Adani had been accused of lying to American investors about payoffs in India. The end of the case came as President Trump has signaled a transactional approach to justice.

title: Two Military Jets Collide in Midair at Idaho Air Show
partialText: Video shared on social media showed the jets striking each other and spinning toward the ground. Four crew members safely ejected before the planes crashed, officials said.

title: Millions Recovered in FIFA Corruption Scandal May Now Be Missing Again Before World Cup
partialText: Ahead of the World Cup, the head of South American soccer faces an ethics complaint he received payments recovered from a 2015 investigation that shook global soccer.

title: Children’s Mental Health Visits Have Shot Up, Research Shows
partialText: Doctor’s visits for children’s anxiety rose by more than 250 percent over 10 years, according to a study of nearly two million children.
